guidance: Usually taken on an empty stomach, 30-60 minutes before breakfast, with water only.
reason: Food, coffee, calcium, iron and antacids all reduce how much levothyroxine is absorbed, which makes the dose less reliable.
source_name: FDA label for levothyroxine sodium (Dosage and Administration)

guidance: Separate from dairy, calcium, iron, zinc, magnesium and antacids by at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after the dose.
reason: These minerals bind the antibiotic in the gut (chelation) and can cut absorption enough for the treatment to fail.
spacing_with: dairy, calcium, iron, zinc, magnesium, antacids

guidance: Take with a full glass of water, stay upright for about 30 minutes, and separate from dairy, antacids and iron by 2 hours.
reason: Tetracyclines bind minerals, and the capsule can irritate or ulcerate the food pipe if taken lying down or with too little water.
source_name: FDA label for doxycycline (Dosage and Administration)

guidance: Usually taken with or just after food, with a full glass of water.
reason: Food reduces stomach irritation. NSAIDs can still cause ulcers and bleeding even when taken with food.
source_name: FDA NSAID class labelling (Dosage and Administration)

guidance: Usually taken with meals, often the evening meal for the first dose.
reason: Taking it with food reduces the nausea and diarrhoea that are common when starting metformin.
source_name: FDA label for metformin hydrochloride (Dosage and Administration)

guidance: Usually taken with food in the morning.
reason: Food limits stomach irritation, and morning dosing matches the body's own cortisol rhythm and disturbs sleep less.
source_name: FDA label for prednisone (Dosage and Administration)

guidance: Usually taken 30-60 minutes before a meal, most often breakfast.
reason: Proton pump inhibitors work on acid pumps that are activated by eating, so they are most effective taken shortly before food.
source_name: FDA label for omeprazole (Dosage and Administration)

reason: Grapefruit blocks the CYP3A4 enzyme in the gut wall, raising statin blood levels and the risk of muscle injury.
source_name: FDA consumer update: grapefruit juice and some drugs don't mix

guidance: Check with a pharmacist before taking grapefruit juice regularly.
reason: Grapefruit can raise blood levels of some calcium channel blockers, increasing dizziness and low blood pressure.
source_name: FDA consumer update: grapefruit juice and some drugs don't mix

guidance: Avoid alcohol during the course and for 3 days after the last dose.
reason: The combination can cause flushing, severe nausea, vomiting and a fast heartbeat (a disulfiram-like reaction).

guidance: Keep your intake of green leafy vegetables steady rather than avoiding them, and tell the anticoagulation clinic before any big diet change.
reason: Vitamin K in those foods opposes warfarin. Consistency matters more than avoidance, because the dose is tuned to your usual diet.
source_name: FDA label for warfarin sodium (Patient Counseling Information)

guidance: Take with food and a full glass of water, sitting or standing upright.
reason: Potassium chloride tablets can irritate or ulcerate the stomach and food pipe if taken dry or lying down.
source_name: FDA label for potassium chloride extended-release (Warnings)

guidance: Avoid alcohol, and do not drive until you know how the medicine affects you.
reason: Alcohol adds to the sedation and slowed breathing these medicines cause.
source_name: FDA opioid and benzodiazepine class labelling (Warnings)

guidance: Limit alcohol, and check every other cold, flu or pain product for paracetamol/acetaminophen before taking one.
reason: Alcohol increases the liver risk from acetaminophen, and accidental double-dosing from combination products is a common cause of overdose.
source_name: FDA Drug Safety Communication on acetaminophen hepatotoxicity

guidance: Can be taken with or without food; taking it at the start of a meal reduces stomach upset, especially with the clavulanate combination.
reason: Absorption is not meaningfully affected by food, but tolerance usually is.
source_name: FDA label for amoxicillin (Dosage and Administration)

guidance: Separate from aluminium- or magnesium-containing antacids by 2 hours.
reason: Those antacids lower the peak blood level of azithromycin.

guidance: Can be taken with or without food, at the same time each day; morning dosing suits most people.
reason: A consistent daily time keeps blood levels steady; some people find these medicines disturb sleep if taken late.
source_name: FDA label for sertraline (Dosage and Administration)

reason: Simvastatin has a short half-life and the body makes most of its cholesterol overnight, so evening dosing is more effective.
source_name: FDA label for simvastatin (Dosage and Administration)
